fullPassage: Perhaps at some point you have seen some mathematical writing and not understood it. (A) The complicated notations that might spring to mind — all those strange dashes, squiggles and letters — are obvious signs, but a lot of those are really quite modern. Mathematics had been going on for a long time before the dashes and squiggles were invented. (B) You would not be the first; rest assured, even professional mathematicians sometimes have to rely on discussions with colleagues to properly understand problems they are looking at. But how do you recognise some writing is mathematical in the first place? (C) Put simply, there has to be something mathematical going on for us to say that it is mathematics. And if we are dealing with writing from a very distant past, in a language that is not familiar to us, from a time even before recorded language, that can be sometimes difficult to recognise.

② notation ←정답: 표기법 — 정의와 정확히 일치
③ equation: 방정식 — 기호 체계가 아닌 수학적 문장
④ formula: 공식 — 기호 체계 자체가 아님

questions.passage: You would not be the first; rest assured, even __________ (profession) mathematicians sometimes have to rely on discussions with colleagues to properly understand problems they are looking at.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 영어로 쓰시오.

det.korean: 명사 mathematicians를 수식하는 형용사 자리이므로 profession의 형용사형 professional이 적절하다.
det.analysis: profession(명사: 직업) → professional(형용사: 전문적인). 빈칸 뒤 mathematicians(명사)를 수식하므로 형용사형 필요.

questions.passage: The complicated notations that might spring to mind — all those strange dashes, squiggles and letters — are obvious signs, but a lot of those are __________ (real) quite modern.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 영어로 쓰시오.

det.korean: 형용사 modern을 수식하는 부사 자리이므로 real의 부사형 really가 적절하다.
det.analysis: real(형용사: 진짜의) → really(부사: 정말로). quite modern을 수식하는 부사 위치.
det.tip: real(형용사) → really(부사): 형용사 앞에서 정도를 강조

questions.passage: Perhaps at some point you have seen some mathematical writing and not understood it. The complicated notations that might spring to mind — all those strange dashes, squiggles and letters — are obvious signs, but a lot of those are really quite modern. Mathematics had been __________ for a long time before the dashes and squiggles were invented. You would not be the first; rest assured, even professional mathematicians sometimes have to rely on discussions with colleagues to properly understand problems they are looking at. But how do you recognise some writing is mathematical in the first place? Put simply, there has to be something mathematical going on for us to say that it is mathematics. And if we are dealing with writing from a very distant past, in a language that is not familiar to us, from a time even before recorded language, that can be sometimes difficult to recognise.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: '수학이 오랫동안 ________해 왔다'는 맥락에서 '계속되다'를 뜻하는 going on이 적절하다. Mathematics had been going on for a long time.
det.analysis:
① dealing with: 다루다 — '수학이 오랫동안 다루고 있었다'는 의미 불완전
② looking at: 보다 — '수학이 오랫동안 보고 있었다'는 의미 부적절
③ going on ←정답: 계속되다 — 수학이 오랫동안 지속됨
④ spring to: 떠오르다 — '수학이 오랫동안 떠오르고 있었다'는 의미 부적절
det.tip: go on(계속되다) — Mathematics had been going on for a long time

You would not be the first; __________, even professional mathematicians sometimes have to rely on discussions with colleagues to properly understand problems they are looking at. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: '당신이 처음은 아닐 것이다; ________, 전문 수학자들도 때때로 동료와의 논의에 의존한다'는 맥락에서, 안심시키는 표현인 rest assured(안심하세요)가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
① rest assured ←정답: 안심하세요 — 위로/안심의 맥락에 적합
② quite modern: 꽤 현대적인 — 세미콜론 뒤 삽입 표현으로 부적절
③ long time: 오랜 시간 — 세미콜론 뒤 삽입 표현으로 부적절
④ in the first place: 애초에 — 뒤 내용(전문가도 의존한다)과 연결 부적절
det.tip: rest assured(안심하세요) — 수학을 이해 못 하는 게 당신만의 문제가 아니라는 위로
